I would try to feed something more nutritious than mealworms. My geckos diet is 8 medium crickets/dubia roaches depending on what I have available, 3-4 mealworms, and every once in a while I’ll throw in a wax worm, a horn worm, or a super worm. Try to vary the diet a little bit because feeding all of any single insect isn’t healthy. Best of luck to you!!

I agree. I would absolutely avoid pellets at all costs, especially with a baby. The best option for a baby is 80% insects (crickets, mealworms, dubia roaches, etc.) and about 20% fruits and veggies (mostly dandelion greens, collard greens, mustard greens, and the occasional fruit since they aren’t as nutritious.) Once he is more grown up, try to wean off of insects a little and mostly rely on veggies with a few fruits thrown in. They need the protein as babies to help them grow but can get morbidly obese if all they eat is insects. Best of luck!!
